---
title: Build an app with Swift
description: Build an iPhone and Mac app that lists and adds the books in your library, keeps working without a connection, and sends its changes when the server is back.
---

- **You'll build** Shelf, a SwiftUI app for iPhone and Mac that lists and adds the books in your library.
- **You need** your own Marfa instance at `http://localhost:8600` with the CLI signed in, as the [Quickstart](/quickstart) leaves you, and Xcode 27 on a Mac with Apple silicon.
- **You'll have** an app that reads from a working copy on the device, so it keeps working when the server can't be reached.

<Steps paged>
<Step>

### Create the project

1. In Xcode, choose **File** > **New** > **Project**, then **Multiplatform** > **App**. Name it `Shelf`, and leave **Storage** set to **None**.
2. Choose **File** > **Add Package Dependencies**, enter `https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa-swift`, and add the `Marfa` product to the `Shelf` target.
3. In the target's **Build Settings**, set **Excluded Architectures** for **Any iOS Simulator SDK** to `x86_64`. Marfa's core is built for Apple silicon only.
4. In the target's **Signing & Capabilities**, under **App Sandbox**, turn on **Outgoing Connections (Client)**, so the Mac app can reach the server.
5. In the target's **Info** tab, under **URL Types**, add a type with **URL Schemes** set to `com.example.shelf`, where the browser hands the sign-in back to the app.

Press Command-B to check that the project builds.

</Step>
<Step>

### Open the working copy

Choose **File** > **New** > **File from Template**, choose **Swift File**, and name it `Library.swift`. Add the class that holds the app's state:

```swift title="Library.swift"
import AuthenticationServices
import Marfa
import SwiftUI

@MainActor @Observable
final class Library {
    private(set) var books: LiveQuery<Rows<Item>>?
    private(set) var queue: LiveQuery<[QueuedWrite]>?
    private(set) var message = ""
    private var copy: WorkingCopy?
    private var opening = false

    func open(signingInWith session: WebAuthenticationSession) async {
        // Each Mac window runs this; only the first opens the store.
        guard copy == nil, !opening else { return }
        opening = true
        defer { opening = false }
        do {
            let serverURL = URL(string: "http://localhost:8600")!
            let auth = try Authorization(
                server: serverURL,
                client: .init(
                    name: "Shelf",
                    redirect: URL(string: "com.example.shelf:/signed-in"),
                    scopes: ["core.media.book:read", "core.media.book:write", "edge.references:write"]),
                service: "com.example.shelf")
            let credential: Credential
            if let kept = try auth.credential() {
                credential = kept
            } else {
                credential = try await auth.signIn(using: session)
            }
            let folder = URL.applicationSupportDirectory.appending(path: "Shelf")
            try FileManager.default.createDirectory(at: folder, withIntermediateDirectories: true)
            let copy = try await WorkingCopy.open(
                store: folder.appending(path: "books.sqlite"),
                server: try Server(url: serverURL, credential: credential))
            self.copy = copy
            books = LiveQuery(copy, reading: .list(ListFilters(types: ["core.media.book"])))
            queue = LiveQuery(copy, reading: .queue)
            await sync()
        } catch { message = error.localizedDescription }
    }

    func sync() async {
        guard let copy else { return }
        do {
            if try await copy.status().hydration != .complete {
                _ = try await copy.hydrate(types: ["core.media.book"], tier: .library)
            }
            _ = try await copy.queue.drain()
            message = ""
        } catch { message = error.localizedDescription }
    }
}
```

**The app signs in as itself and never holds a key.** It asks to read and write books, and to link them for the next tutorial; the owner approves those scopes in the browser, and the keychain keeps the sign-in. [Sign in](/swift-sdk/server-calls#sign-in) lists the other ways.

`open()` keeps the [working copy](/build/devices) in a SQLite file in Application Support. The first `sync()` fills the empty copy with every book in your library, and each `sync()` sends the writes waiting in the queue. Each `LiveQuery` **reads the copy again whenever it changes**, so a view that shows it stays current, and while one is held, the copy follows the instance by itself.

</Step>
<Step>

### Show your books

Replace the contents of `ShelfApp.swift`, so every window shares one `Library`:

```swift title="ShelfApp.swift"
import SwiftUI

@main
struct ShelfApp: App {
    @State private var library = Library()

    var body: some Scene {
        WindowGroup { ContentView(library: library) }
    }
}
```

Replace the contents of `ContentView.swift` with a list of the books, a **Sync** button and a line for errors, which opens the copy when it appears:

```swift title="ContentView.swift"
import AuthenticationServices
import Marfa
import SwiftUI

struct ContentView: View {
    let library: Library
    @Environment(\.webAuthenticationSession) private var session

    var body: some View {
        NavigationStack {
            List {
                ForEach(library.books?.value ?? []) { book in
                    LabeledContent(book.title ?? "Untitled", value: book.properties["author"]?.string ?? "")
                }
            }
            .navigationTitle("Shelf")
            .toolbar {
                Button("Sync", systemImage: "arrow.clockwise") { Task { await library.sync() } }
            }
            .safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom) {
                Text(library.message).font(.caption).foregroundStyle(.secondary)
            }
        }
        .task { await library.open(signingInWith: session) }
    }
}
```

Each row shows a book's `title` and `author`, two fields of the `core.media.book` [type](/build/items-and-types).

Choose **My Mac** or an iPhone simulator as the run destination, and press Command-R. A simulator reaches `localhost` on your Mac; an iPhone needs an address it reaches over HTTPS, set as `serverURL` ([Give your instance an address](/run/address)). Your instance's sign-in page opens: sign in as the owner, and approve Shelf. The list shows your books, read from the working copy. The next run signs in by itself.

</Step>
<Step>

### Add a book

Add these two functions inside `Library`:

```swift title="Library.swift"
    func add(title: String, author: String) async {
        await write { copy in
            try await copy.items.create(
                Draft(type: "core.media.book", properties: [
                    "title": .string(title), "author": .string(author), "progress": "planned",
                ]))
        }
    }

    private func write(_ change: (WorkingCopy) async throws -> QueuedWrite) async {
        guard let copy else { return }
        do {
            _ = try await change(copy)
            _ = try await copy.queue.drain()
        } catch { message = error.localizedDescription }
    }
```

`items.create` **returns at once**: the book is in the working copy, and the write waits in the queue until `drain()` sends it.

Add fields for a book at the end of `ContentView.swift`, and put `NewBookFields(library: library)` first inside the `List`:

```swift title="ContentView.swift"
struct NewBookFields: View {
    let library: Library
    @State private var title = ""
    @State private var author = ""

    var body: some View {
        Section("New book") {
            TextField("Title", text: $title)
            TextField("Author", text: $author)
            Button("Add to Shelf") {
                let (added, by) = (title, author)
                (title, author) = ("", "")
                Task { await library.add(title: added, author: by) }
            }
            .disabled(title.isEmpty)
        }
    }
}
```

Run the app, add `Bleak House` by `Charles Dickens`, and choose **Add to Shelf**. The book appears at once. List the newest book in a terminal to see that it reached your instance:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa items list --type core.media.book --limit 1
```

```text
id                                    type             when                      title
01a1f134-05b9-70a9-ae2b-43825493170b  core.media.book  2026-11-19T00:28:00.830Z  Bleak House

```

</Terminal>

</Step>
<Step>

### Work without a connection

Add the answered writes and a function that takes them, inside `Library`:

```swift title="Library.swift"
    private(set) var answers: [QueuedWrite] = []

    func takeAnswers() async {
        guard let copy else { return }
        do { answers = try await copy.queue.takeAnswered() + answers }
        catch { message = error.localizedDescription }
    }
```

`takeAnswered()` returns the answered writes and clears them from the queue **in one step**, so the app shows each answer once, even with two windows open. A refused write that carried content stays in the queue until you discard it.

Add a section for the queue and one for the answers at the end of `ContentView.swift`, and put `ChangesSection(library: library)` last inside the `List`:

```swift title="ContentView.swift"
struct ChangesSection: View {
    let library: Library

    var body: some View {
        Section("Changes") {
            ForEach(library.queue?.value ?? [], id: \.id) { Text(describe($0)) }
            Button("Take Answers") { Task { await library.takeAnswers() } }
        }
        Section("Answered") {
            ForEach(library.answers, id: \.id) { Text(describe($0)) }
        }
    }

    private func describe(_ write: QueuedWrite) -> String {
        switch write.verdict {
        case nil: write.waiting ? "Waiting for an earlier change" : "Waiting to send"
        case .accepted: "Sent"
        case .merged(let fields): "Merged \(fields.joined(separator: ", ")) with a newer change"
        case .conflicted: "Changed elsewhere too. Your text is in a conflicted copy."
        case .refused(let refusal): "Refused: \(refusal.message ?? refusal.reason)"
        case .blocked, .dead: "Stopped. Needs attention."
        }
    }
}
```

A write has no `verdict` until the instance answers it. [Verdicts](/build/devices#verdicts) explains each one.

Run the app. **Changes** shows Bleak House as Sent; choose **Take Answers**, and it moves to **Answered**. Then stop the server:

```bash
marfa server stop
```

Add `Middlemarch` by `George Eliot`. It appears in the list, and **Changes** shows Waiting to send. Start the server with `marfa server start`: **the copy sends the write by itself** once the server answers, and **Changes** shows Sent. **Sync** sends it at once.

</Step>
